sessions.title: Repository foundation (turn 1), operations desk foundation and first slice (turn 2), hosting plan and Claude agent lab (turn 3), Ghost-free publishing with agents under policy (turn 4)
sessions.agent: Claude Code (cloud session) for Paul Phillips
sessions.summary: Unpacked and audited the launch packet; installed and verified the toolchain; built dev log, delivery tracking, validators, CI and the Pages project hub; researched current vendor facts; wrote the foundation planning brief for the next turn's plan mode. Turn 2 (v0.2.0): built the operations desk foundation (SC-005) and its first vertical slice (SC-006 pitch intake with source and rights records, SC-007 editorial queue with Ghost references, first part of SC-009 agent gateway) on local Supabase, with database policy, unit, end-to-end, accessibility and bundle-secret tests. Turn 3 (v0.3.0): verified hosting and running costs (Supabase Pro plus Cloud Run and Cloud Storage), proposed ADR-004 for automated Ghost drafts with one-click human publishing, added a production container image with a CI smoke test, and built a Claude-powered agent lab whose real runs wait for an API key. Turn 4 (v0.4.0): the founders chose a Ghost-free start (ADR-005). Stories are written in the desk with revisions and published as our own static site (Firebase Hosting; Kit for the newsletter). Agents may publish their own proposals only inside owner switches and database-enforced checks, and people are never blocked. The cost plan drops to about $1 a month to start, with prices verified on official pages. Turn 4, security hardening (v0.4.1): an independent review of agent publishing found one High, four Medium and three Low problems. All are fixed with regression tests: rebuilds use each story's published revision, claim tokens fence every step, the newsletter is sent at most once per job, agent jobs are re-checked when they run, refusals are recorded and budgeted, and agent text is checked as readers see it. Eight more problems found while fixing them are fixed too. Turn 5 (v0.5.0): the desk (Cloud Run, us-west1) and the public site (Firebase Hosting) went live as a preview on Paul's Supabase and Google Cloud projects, with preview banners and noindex everywhere, a hardened sign-in configuration and an owner account for Paul; real-email sign-in and the first publication are the next live checks. Turn 6 (v0.6.0): the preview site now carries seven clearly labelled sample stories (a guarded is_sample flag that only an operator can set, and that the builder refuses on a non-preview site) and About and How we work pages drafted from the founders' copy. The desk gained a publishing sweep endpoint that accepts only a Google-signed token from one service account; the Cloud Scheduler job that would call it is left to Paul. The sample removal path and an owner's update of a live sample were rehearsed locally; a publication by the desk service on Cloud Run is the next live check. Turn 7 (v0.7.0, v0.7.1): the public site gained photographs (six credited public-domain samples; the desk makes AVIF and WebP renditions, strips metadata and pins each image at publish) and a motion and depth system on GSAP ScrollTrigger (layered parallax, reveals that reverse on scroll-back, raised and recessed surfaces lit from one direction), tuned from design tokens v0.2 with presets, a reader switch, reduced-motion and no-JavaScript support. Story images are tied to cleared rights records and agents never publish them (ADR-006, Proposed). Red-teaming the desk's own container with Cloud Run's limits found that a 24-megapixel upload would crash the live desk and that uploads over 10 MB were cut off; v0.7.1 bounds image processing's memory, raises the body limit, names HEIC files, versions the stylesheet's fonts and art, and runs the live desk with 1 GiB (revision sc-desk-00005-dw7). An image upload and a publication by the live desk are the next live checks. Turn 8 (v0.7.2): asked whether images were posted at native size, a live audit showed readers never receive originals and every browser already took the smallest covering rendition; phones denser than 2.5x are now served as if 2x, halving their image bytes (home page 369 to 188 KB) with no visible difference, and the audit became a repository tool (audit:images).
